A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SAM-REF research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and references support a reliable comparison. All pages were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAM-REF benchmark results, component and block-count ablations, latency measurements, and qualitative segmentation examples in Sections 4–6.

after.justification: v3 reports original SAM-REF benchmark results, revised ablations, qualitative examples, and an additional computation-cost comparison in Sections 4–6.

M1.justification: Beyond renaming GlobalDiff/PatchDiff as GFR/LFR, the stated selector procedure changes. v1 Section 3.4.2 chooses local PatchDiff updates when error regions increase and otherwise uses GlobalDiff; v3 Section 3.5 pastes the local result onto either the previous mask or the globally refined mask. This is a bounded revision to the described inference procedure; the overall SAM-plus-two-refiners design remains.

E1.justification: Both versions use COCO, LVIS, and HQ-Seg and evaluate click-based segmentation on GrabCut, Berkeley, DAVIS, SBD, and HQ-Seg. HQSeg-44K is the renamed existing HQ-Seg collection. Changed training combinations and additional computational measurements do not introduce new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 substantially expands the evaluated comparator set by adding F-BRS, CDNet, EdgeFlow, and AdaptiveClick, each with reported benchmark scores. The principal earlier comparators remain; SAM-HQ/HQ-SAM denotes the same method rather than an additional baseline.

E3.justification: The second training configuration changes from COCO+LVIS+HQ-Seg to HQSeg-only training, replacing the combined-training comparisons and adding HQSeg-trained SAM-REF evaluation on the four mainstream benchmarks. v3 also adds a SAM ViT-H configuration to Table 2 and parameter, FPS, and memory measurements in Table 3. These materially revise experimental conditions, although the 320k/80k training schedule, batch size, and core click metrics remain.

E4.justification: The three component configurations in v1 Table 3 become four explicit mask-pasting controls in v3 Table 4, including an always-paste-onto-previous-mask control; per-configuration SPC is removed. v3 also adds the computation-cost analysis. The block-count study and both qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Both present point estimates without run-to-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Results change across the main comparisons and ablations, alongside substantial added and replaced rows. For COCO+LVIS-trained SAM-REF ViT-H, Table 1 reports DAVIS NoC95 changing from 9.28 to 9.10 and SBD NoC95 from 10.61 to 10.41. Table 2 changes its latency from 6.9 to 5.22 seconds and HQ-SAM's 5-mIoU from 89.95 to 89.45. New baseline and computation results are added; HQSeg-only results replace combined-training results and are not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 adds the explicit thresholded-error ratio definition and decision criterion in Equation 5, where v1 describes error-region growth qualitatively. The local fusion equation also explicitly uses the global-refiner prediction as its reference, replacing v1's SAM-based description. Other added feature-fusion equations largely formalize existing prose; neither version contains theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central accuracy-and-efficiency contribution is retained. v3's introduction replaces v1's specific claim of matching SimpleClick on NoC95 with performance leadership on most metrics. Section 4.2 also corrects the stated exceptions to include both GrabCut and DAVIS, consistent with Table 1.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1's explicit limitations discussion concerning frozen-encoder biases, click-only applicability, and possible extension to other prompts. It adds interpretations of the mask-pasting controls and explains that total SAT latency favors methods that encode the image once. The main image-prompt-synergy explanation remains.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies the selector threshold as 1.1, identifies the ablations' ViT-H/COCO+LVIS/DAVIS configuration, and states the HQSeg validation size of 1,537 samples. Hardware, training iterations, batch size, and embedding caching are retained. The newly disclosed evaluation details do not themselves establish changed underlying settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for F-BRS, CDNet, EdgeFlow, AdaptiveClick, and the Transformer, while removing CFR-ICL and the general Deep Learning reference. CDNet also enters the related-work discussion. The central positioning between early fusion, late fusion, and SAM-based refinement remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and method undergo extensive rewriting, with consistent GFR/LFR/DS terminology and a standalone Dynamic Selector section. Contribution bullets become a summary paragraph, the limitations section disappears, and an acknowledgment is added. The title and author information also change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint layout to two columns. Figures 1 and 2 are substantially redrawn, Figure 4 is recolored and recropped, and tables are reorganized with revised annotations. A computation table is added and the component-ablation table is restructured. Figure 3 retains the same qualitative results.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a more reproducible selector specification, an additional mask-pasting control, broader baseline comparisons, and direct computational-overhead evidence. It also corrects the NoC95 comparison with SimpleClick and substantially clarifies the diagrams. These provide a limited overall quality gain, balanced against the removal of explicit applicability limitations. Revised scores and results under changed training regimes do not independently establish improvement.
